title: What is joint aspiration?
intro: Joint aspiration, or arthrocentesis, is a procedure in which a needle is used to withdraw fluid from a joint. It is done to find the cause of joint swelling or pain, to relieve pressure and sometimes to inject medicine. It is quick and usually done in a doctor's office.

sections.heading: Why it is done
paragraphs: Fluid analysis can identify infection, gout, pseudogout crystals, bleeding or inflammatory arthritis. Removing fluid from a very swollen joint relieves pain and improves movement. A suspected joint infection is an emergency, and aspiration is needed urgently to prevent permanent damage.

sections.heading: How it is done
paragraphs: The skin is cleaned and may be numbed with local anaesthetic or cooling spray. Using a sterile technique, the doctor inserts a needle into the joint, sometimes guided by ultrasound, and draws out fluid. If wanted, a corticosteroid or other medicine is injected through the same needle. The procedure takes a few minutes.

sections.heading: What fluid shows
paragraphs: Normal joint fluid is clear and thick. Cloudy fluid suggests inflammation or infection, bloody fluid suggests injury or bleeding disorder, and crystals in the fluid indicate gout or pseudogout. The sample is sent to the laboratory for cell counts, crystals and bacterial culture.

sections.heading: Aftercare and risks
paragraphs: Rest the joint for a day or two and avoid heavy use. A little soreness is common. Risks are uncommon and include infection, bleeding and damage to cartilage. Contact a doctor if you develop fever, increasing pain, redness, warmth or swelling after the procedure. Tell the doctor if you take blood thinners.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: Some results are available within hours, others, such as culture, take days. The doctor explains the findings and the treatment, for example antibiotics for infection, or medicines for gout.

examples.title: Preparing
examples.text: Imagine you have a swollen knee. You could tell the doctor about blood thinners and note when swelling began and whether you had fever.

examples.title: Aftercare
examples.text: Suppose you had fluid removed from your knee. You might rest it for a day and watch for warmth, redness or fever.
